blocks.x: Profiling, scheduling and mixed precision often deliver more than the next node.
HPC throughput is a software story before a hardware story. GPU partitioning and storage tiering fix the bottlenecks scientists actually feel.
Reproducible containers make simulation results defensible in regulation and review.
Cloud burst extends capacity without capital — under data-governance rules.
Where it breaks in practice: spectacle: formulations chosen for the press release rather than the problem class, benchmarked against weak classical baselines that do not survive review.
The strongest counter-case, stated fairly: the formulation-first thesis can hide behind rigor while the classical baseline quietly improves. Benchmarks are re-run on a schedule, not once.

In delivery, this thesis becomes a specific discipline: we treat advanced compute as a tool with a contract — bounded problem classes, measured speedups, and a classical baseline the CFO can read. Every program in the Quantum & Advanced Compute domain carries the same obligations — a signed baseline, named gate criteria, and evidence generated by running the system rather than preparing for a meeting.
Bring HPC throughput is a software story before a hardware story to a 45-minute briefing with the practice lead — your metric, our method, and an honest read on feasibility.
